title: The Exodus from Egypt and the Red Sea Crossing
summary: After the Passover, Israel leaves Rameses on the 15th day of the first month, 430 years "to the selfsame day" after the promise, and crosses the Red Sea (Exod 12–14).
description: CFAH-6 frames its Egyptian reconstruction as running "from the Dispersion in 2191 BC until the Exodus in 1491 BC" and finds the deaths of Concharis and Merenre II at 1491 BC ±6 months; the year itself is CFAH-1 Table 1's Ussher-Jones baseline.

sorting_basis.note: Tier 1: CFAH anchor point: 1491 BC (AP-109, OSF preprint CFAH-19). Sort changed by the CFAH pass (2026-10-18): was cfah-table1 1491 BC.

chronologies.citation: Griffith & White, "CFAH-19: The Historical Ice Age," OSF preprint v1.0 (8 Jul 2026), doi:10.17605/OSF.IO/A5G6X, file CFAH-19_Historical_Ice_Age_v1.0.pdf, p. 15 ("the year of the Exodus in 1491 BC, new Anchor Point #109")
chronologies.note: CFAH-19 frames this as the cataclysm around the Exodus; the year matches CFAH-1 Table 1.

chronologies.citation: Griffith & White, "Chronological Framework of Ancient History. 1: Problem, Data, and Methodology," ARJ 15 (2022): 377–390, section "Our Assumptions (Declared Biases)", Table 1 "Biblically derived dates from Ussher and Jones"
chronologies.note: CFAH-1 Table 1 (Ussher-Jones biblical baseline adopted by CFAH); not a triangulated anchor point. CFAH-6 Introduction: "from the Dispersion in 2191 BC until the Exodus in 1491 BC".

chronologies.date: 2513 AM, 1491 BC (the year of the EXODUS)
chronologies.citation: Jones, Chart No. 1 "Creation to Jesus Christ" (© 1993), line "2513 AM 1491 BC the year of the EXODUS - Moses"; Chronology of the Old Testament (15th ed., 2002), Chart One §B, p. 24 ("1012 + 479 = 1491 BC")

chronologies.date: 15th day of the 1st month; at the end of the 430 years; Solomon's Temple begun in the 480th year after
2513 AM, 1491 BC; 15th day of 1st month = Tuesday 5 May (Julian)
chronologies.citation: Ussher, Annals of the World, Fourth Age §190 (paragraph numbering of the modern transcription)
chronologies.note: Red Sea crossing at Pihahiroth narrated in §190 (camp 4).

chronologies.citation: Jordan, "Egypt in Biblical History," Biblical Chronology 5:8 (December 1993), chart "Anno Mundi / B.C. (SBC) / B.C. (CCC)" at the start of the article
chronologies.note: Day: 15th day of the 1st month of 2513 ("Day 15: The exodus from Egypt"), Pentateuch Part 5 (BC 6:7) §16. Same chart: CCC 1447 B.C. B.C. year is Jordan's "SBC" (strictest Biblical chronology), which takes Daniel's 70 weeks literally from Cyrus (456 B.C. instead of the conventional 536 B.C.); not comparable one-to-one with Ussher/CFAH B.C. years. Restated in Jordan, From Creation to Solomon (Studies in Biblical Chronology No. 2, 2001), ch. 11, p. 44: "The Exodus took place in 2513" and p. 51 list "2513 - Exodus from Egypt"; and in A Chronological and Calendrical Commentary on the Pentateuch (No. 3, 2001), ch. 17 "Chronology of the Plagues & Exodus", p. 43: "1st Month (March-April 2513) ... Day 15: The exodus from Egypt".

chronologies.date: "the exodus took place 857 years after the Flood"
chronologies.citation: Jordan, The Law of the Covenant (Institute for Christian Economics, 1984), ch. 2 "The Law and the Redemption of Israel", p. 44
chronologies.note: Interval only, as printed (n. 25 cites Anstey). Not converted to AM here.

chronologies.date: 1497 B.C. Exodus Event occurred in 2513 AM, 430 yrs. after Abram entered Canaan
chronologies.citation: Anno Mundi Chronology Studies (unnamed compiler; a compilation of James B. Jordan's system), p. 3, chart "Genesis 12 – 25 Chronology of Abraham’s Life"
chronologies.note: Agrees with Jordan's own published AM 2513. The compilation's B.C. year (1497) is AM subtracted from 4010 (its own convention: Creation 4010 B.C.); Jordan's own SBC B.C. figures differ (here 1417 B.C.). Display only; never converted or used for sorting.

chronologies.note: The Memorandum lists intervals 1656, 0292, 0500, 0480, 0410, 0432, 0134 against seven rows; the row/number pairing is read from OCR column order and should be checked against the page scan.

Morecraft, A Christian Survey of World History, p. 14 (PDF p. 23)
Raleigh, The History of the World (1617, EEBO-TCP A10357), Chronological Table, sig. 784a
chronologies.note: Year cell "3196 2514 1". The third printed figure 1 is the column "Exodus", not a length. To the Reader (sig. 780b): the Julian Period exceeds the yeere of the World by 682. Book II, ch. III, §I, sig. 174a prints "2514. to Codoman, or after our account, 2513." Book II, ch. IIII, §I, sig. 184a prints the Passover "in the yeere of the World 2514." The table row entered is "The Passeouer." at World 2514. 2513 is not given a second year.

chronologies.date: about twenty years before the Israelites went out of Egypt
chronologies.citation: Shuckford, The Sacred and Profane History of the World Connected, 5th ed., revised by James Creighton (London: William Baynes, 1819), vol. 1, Book V, p. 306 (facsimile PDF p. 402)
chronologies.note: The twenty years are counted from Danaus at A. M. 2494, “as I have placed it”. He does not print an Anno Mundi for the Exodus on this page. None is derived.
